- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

# Llama Stack GA-Readiness Assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps
between current Llama Stack Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. It produces
the definitive GA scope that all Llama Stack stability, hardening, and support
posture work is sized against. Until this assessment lands, the size of the
stability and hardening work remains an estimate (strategy Open Question 1).

## Scope

- Systematically inventory gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar
  across the four assessment dimensions named in the strategy:
  - API stability (which parts of the published OpenAI-compatible API surface
    and LlamaStackDistribution CRD behavior are unstable or undocumented)
  - Upgrade paths (what breaks when moving between recent TP releases)
  - Scale limits (documented and observed limits of supported distributions)
  - Error handling (failure modes, error surfacing, recovery behavior)
- Consolidate scattered TP feedback from support tickets into the gap
  inventory.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: each gap classified
  (must-fix-for-GA vs. acceptable-with-follow-up), with the remediation work
  itemized so downstream implementation epics can be sized and scoped.
- Identify which gaps fall into API stabilization work, which into general
  hardening, and which constrain the supported configuration matrix and SLO
  targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists covering all four assessment dimensions (API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with each gap
  traceable to evidence (source inspection, upgrade testing, or support
  ticket).
- TP feedback from support tickets is consolidated and reflected in the
  inventory.
- A definitive GA scope document is produced that downstream stability,
  hardening, and support-posture work can be scoped from, with each GA-blocking
  gap assigned to a remediation area.
- Gaps that inform the supported configuration matrix and SLO targets are
  explicitly called out.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is the
  assessment itself.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantee and Tested Upgrade Path

## Description

This epic delivers the API stability guarantee that GA requires for the
Llama Stack published API surface: versioned APIs, a deprecation policy, and
a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface (the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD behavior exposed to users) so GA customers can
  build against a stable contract.
- Author and publish a deprecation policy defining how API changes are
  signaled, how long deprecated surfaces remain supported, and what customers
  must do when upgrading.
- Implement and test an upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the GA
  release, including migration of existing LlamaStackDistribution resources.
- Stabilize the specific API behaviors flagged as GA-blocking by the
  GA-readiness assessment.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green for all changes in the
  Llama Stack midstream repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published APIs are versioned, and the versioning scheme is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published and covers signaling, support windows for
  deprecated surfaces, and upgrade obligations.
- An upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA release is
  exercised by automated tests, with documented migration steps for any
  breaking change.
- API behaviors identified as GA-blocking by the GA-readiness assessment are
  stabilized or explicitly covered by the deprecation policy.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream repo is green with
  these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases.
- HLR-1 (P0, partial): stabilization targets are the API-stability gaps
  inventoried by the GA-readiness assessment.

# Llama Stack GA Gap Remediation

## Description

This epic closes the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment inventories
beyond API stability — scale limits, error handling, and any other GA-blocking
findings — bringing Llama Stack TP quality up to the GA bar.

## Scope

- Remediate the GA-blocking gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment,
  scoped to the definitive GA scope that assessment produces. Expected gap
  areas per the strategy:
  - Scale limits: raise, document, or enforce limits for supported
    distributions so they meet GA expectations.
  - Error handling: improve failure modes, error surfacing, and recovery
    behavior to GA quality.
  - Any other assessment findings classified as must-fix-for-GA.
- Re-verify each remediated gap against its assessment evidence to confirm
  closure.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green for all changes in the
  Llama Stack midstream repo.

The concrete work items in this epic are defined by the assessment outcome;
the epic exists so that assessment-found remediation has a planned home
rather than being discovered late.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every gap classified as must-fix-for-GA by the GA-readiness assessment
  (outside API stability, which is handled by the API stability guarantee
  work) is remediated or explicitly re-classified with recorded justification.
- Each remediation is verified against the evidence that originally recorded
  the gap.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream repo is green with
  these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0, partial): closing the gaps inventoried by the GA-readiness
  assessment — the assessment defines the scope, this epic delivers the
  remediation.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place that Llama Stack GA
requires: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported
configuration matrix.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for supported Llama Stack distributions
  (availability and operational targets appropriate to the GA commitment),
  informed by the scale limits and configurations validated by the
  GA-readiness assessment.
- Author the backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for how long, and
  how fixes relate to the versioned API surface and deprecation policy
  delivered by the API stability guarantee work.
- Produce the supported configuration matrix: the distribution
  configurations, provider combinations, and deployment sizes that are
  supported at GA, aligned with the scale-limit findings of the GA-readiness
  assessment.
- Obtain ratification of the SLO targets and backport policy from the
  support organization and product owners (these are organizational
  commitments, not merely documents).

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented for supported distributions and ratified by the
  supporting organization.
- A backport policy is published, consistent with the versioned API surface
  and deprecation policy.
- A supported configuration matrix is published, covering the configurations
  and scale ranges validated as GA-ready.
- The posture documents reflect the definitive GA scope from the GA-readiness
  assessment rather than TP-era assumptions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

# Promote TrustyAI Guardrails Integration to Supported

## Description

This epic makes safety guardrails via TrustyAI a supported, documented
integration for GA Llama Stack distributions, removing the experimental-flag
status that Tech Preview carried.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental/TP opt-in gating around the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration so it is part of supported GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Wire the integration as a supported safety provider configuration for
  Llama Stack distributions, building on the existing experimental
  integration as the reference implementation.
- Add the integration to the supported configuration surface (documented,
  tested configuration rather than an experimental flag).
- Include test coverage demonstrating the guardrails integration working
  against a GA distribution configuration.
- Update in-repo references and configuration defaults that describe the
  integration as experimental, where those changes fall out of the same code
  change (substantive user-facing documentation is handled by the GA
  documentation uplift work).

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails are configurable as a supported (non-experimental)
  integration in GA Llama Stack distributions.
- No TP opt-in flag is required to enable the guardrails integration in a GA
  distribution.
- Automated tests cover the supported integration path.
- The existing Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack midstream repo is
  green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# TrustyAI Guardrails Integration Validation and Support Readiness

## Description

This epic covers the TrustyAI team's validation of the TrustyAI guardrails
integration with Llama Stack GA distributions and the TrustyAI-side readiness
to support that integration at GA. TrustyAI itself is already a Stable (GA)
component with no indicated code changes; this work ensures the component
keeps working correctly as the guardrails backend for Llama Stack GA and that
the TrustyAI team can stand behind the supported designation.

## Scope

- Validate TrustyAI guardrails behavior when used as the safety provider for
  Llama Stack GA distribution configurations (the promoted, non-experimental
  integration).
- Verify compatibility across the supported TrustyAI service versions and
  configurations that the GA support posture commits to.
- Confirm TrustyAI-side support readiness for the integration: monitoring
  signals, known-limitation inventory, and escalation path alignment with the
  production support posture.
- Produce the TrustyAI-side validation findings and support sign-off as the
  deliverable that backs the "supported integration" claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails are validated working against Llama Stack GA
  distribution configurations, with results recorded.
- Compatibility with the supported TrustyAI configurations is confirmed and
  documented.
- TrustyAI team support sign-off for the integration is recorded, including
  any known limitations.
- Validation findings are handed off to the GA documentation uplift so the
  documented integration reflects verified behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration for GA distributions — this epic provides the TrustyAI-side
  validation and support commitment behind that guarantee.

# Enable Llama Stack Management by Default in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic makes the Dashboard's Llama Stack management capability enabled by
default for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate that
currently hides it.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management feature from opt-in (TP gate)
  to enabled by default for entitled clusters.
- Gate the default enablement on cluster entitlement so only entitled
  clusters get the capability, using the Dashboard's existing per-component
  feature flag and defaults mechanism (OdhDashboardConfig).
- Preserve an explicit off-switch in configuration so administrators can
  disable the capability for troubleshooting (rollback path for the default
  flip).
- Update feature-flag defaults and any navigation/entry-point conditioning
  that referenced the TP opt-in, where those changes fall out of the same
  code change.
- Keep the existing Konflux build pipeline green for the Dashboard repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default configuration, Llama Stack management
  is available in the Dashboard with no opt-in action required.
- On clusters without entitlement, the capability remains hidden.
- The capability can be explicitly disabled via configuration by an
  administrator (rollback for the default change).
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Dashboard repo is green with these
  changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

## Notes

Release coordination: this change exposes Llama Stack management to all
entitled clusters, so it should ship in step with the Llama Stack GA
graduation rather than ahead of it. This is a release-train coordination
point, not a code dependency — the Dashboard change builds against the
already-existing LlamaStackDistribution CR surface and is otherwise
independent.
